title: OAuth 2.0 vs SAML 2.0: Which One Scales? ⚡
fb_caption:
OAuth 2.0 vs SAML 2.0: Which Architecture Actually Scales in Production? ⚡

🚀 Throughput: OAuth 2.0 generally handles higher volumes due to its token-based approach, ideal for APIs and mobile apps.
📉 Latency: SAML can introduce higher latency with XML parsing and redirects, whereas OAuth 2.0 is often faster.
✅ Consistency: SAML offers robust federation capabilities but can be more complex to manage across diverse systems.
💥 Failure Modes: OAuth 2.0's distributed nature can offer better resilience, while SAML's centralized trust can be a single point of failure.
⚙️ Operational Overhead: OAuth 2.0 is typically simpler to implement and manage for modern web/mobile apps.

Recommendation: For most modern applications, especially APIs and mobile, OAuth 2.0 offers superior scalability and developer experience. SAML remains powerful for enterprise SSO scenarios.
